This invariant has consequences that ecosystem participants need to plan for:

-- **Agent skills, the upgrade instructions, and any other tooling we ship alongside the framework version in lockstep with it.** A skill installed at the same time as `@internal/postgres@0.8.0` is a `0.8.0` skill and reasons about a `0.8.0` contract. There is no separate skill-version axis to track. This is now physical rather than conventional: the `prisma-8` skill ships inside the `@prisma/orm-postgres`, `@prisma/orm-sqlite` and `@prisma/orm-mongo` tarballs (copied in by each package's `prepack`), and `scripts/set-version.ts` stamps its `metadata.library_version` frontmatter with the version being published. Getting the skill and getting the code are one install, and a consumer can compare the stamp on its synced copy against its installed packages.

Getting the skill and getting the code are one install, and a consumer can compare the stamp on its synced copy against its installed packages.

- **Extension authors that depend on internal framework packages must pin those dependencies to the framework version their consumers will use.** If your extension depends on `@internal/sql-core` (an internal framework package), publish each version of your extension targeting one specific Prisma 8 minor and pin to it exactly (`"@internal/sql-core": "0.8.0"`, not `"^0.8.0"`). Internal packages do not promise inter-minor compatibility — `0.8.x` and `0.9.x` may have incompatible internals even when the user-visible surface looks similar. The extension's published version range communicates which framework minor it targets.

- **Internal packages are never published, but they still version in lockstep** so a contributor cloning the repo at any commit sees one consistent answer to "what version is this code?" The `private: true` flag means `pnpm publish` skips them.

The numbered prefixes serve two purposes:
+A minimal demo showing how to use `@prisma/orm-mysql`, the one package a MySQL
+application installs. It has a PSL contract with two models, a relation and an
+enum, and a committed migration written by `prisma migration plan`.
+MySQL support is early, and this example grows with it. Today it shows the
+control plane: the contract emits, the committed migration applies to an empty
+MySQL database, `db verify` and `db sign` pass, and planning again from the
+unchanged contract writes nothing. Reads, writes and MariaDB will be added here
+as each lands, and each is done only when this example runs it in CI.
+You need a MySQL 8 server and an empty application database for the example.
+The repository's `docker-compose.yaml` starts a server on port 3307; create the
+`prisma_demo` database on it before running anything. `MYSQL_URL` must name
+that database, never MySQL's own `mysql` system database, or the CLI creates
+docker compose exec mysql mysql -uroot -proot -e 'CREATE DATABASE prisma_demo'
+pnpm db:migrate                             # applies migrations/ to the database
+pnpm db:verify                              # checks the database matches the contract
+pnpm db:sign                                # records the contract the database now satisfies
+`db sign` writes `migrations/app/refs/db.json`, the migration graph's record of
+| `emit:check` | `emit`, then `git diff` | Fails when the committed contract is out of date |
+| `migration:plan` | `prisma migration plan` | Writes a new migration under `migrations/app/` when the contract has changed; name it with `pnpm migration:plan --name <name>` |
+| `db:migrate` | `prisma db migrate` | Applies the migrations the database does not have yet |
+| `db:verify` | `prisma db verify` | Checks the database's marker and schema against the contract |
+| `db:sign` | `prisma db sign` | Signs a database whose schema satisfies the contract |
+| `test` | `vitest run` | The whole flow against a fresh database at `MYSQL_URL` |
+`pnpm test` uses only the server part of `MYSQL_URL`: it creates a uniquely
+named database on that server, runs `db migrate`, `db verify`, `db sign` and `migration plan` against it
+through the `prisma` CLI, and drops the database. Without `MYSQL_URL` the tests
+plus an index on `Post.authorId` and the foreign key to `User`. The PSL enum
+`Role` becomes a native MySQL `enum` column, so the database enforces its
+members. `String` becomes `varchar(191)`, because MySQL cannot put a unique
+index on a `text` column without a key length.
+- `prisma.config.ts` — CLI config; reads the connection from `MYSQL_URL`
+- `migrations/` — the committed migration and its contract snapshot
+- `test/database.ts` — creates and drops a database for each test run
